title: Weekday Release Whisper and Ops Crib (rough draft)
body:
Purpose:
A terse, practical checklist and week-view for small, low-noise releases (the `Release Whisper` pattern). This is a working crib for on-call, SRE, and the owning eng team to coordinate quick weekday rollouts with minimal blast radius. Keep it short, runable, and copy/pasteable into shift notes.

High-level constraints and intent:
- Target windows: weekdays 10:00–11:30 local region OR 02:00–04:00 UTC for low-traffic components. Avoid peak business hours for customer-facing models.
- Rollouts should aim for incremental exposure: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> global with 15–20 minute observation windows.
- Each step has a single named owner and a defined delta (traffic, config, model variant).
- If any SLO/telemetry threshold is crossed, immediately revert to previous serving variant and open a postmortem link (template below).

Week calendar (rough slotting) 
Mon 2026-06-21:
  - 09:30 PT: preflight sync (15m) — owners: Riley, Samir
  - 10:00 PT: preflight smoke on staging -> signoff
  - 10:30 PT: 1% canary roll (owner: feature-owner)
  - 10:50 PT: observe telemetry window (20m)
  - 11:10 PT: decision point -> progress to 10% or rollback (owner: SRE on-call)

Tue 2026-06-22:
  - 02:00 UTC: midnight micropatch for infra (if needed)
  - 02:30 UTC: validate shard routing and KV cache hit rates

Wed 2026-06-23:
  - 11:00 PT: targeted model-variant bump for dedicated pool (owner: Elena)
  - Post-deploy: run quick-evals on saved prompt set A (local scripts below)

Quick checklist: copy these into Slack/shift notes before starting
- [ ] Announce: #release-ops + #sre with channel, short TL;DR, link to quick dashboard
- [ ] Confirm preflight smoke tests pass on staging: smoke-staging.sh --suite=core
- [ ] Snapshot current model and route config: infra snapshot --prefix=pre-whisper-YYYYMMDD-HHMM
- [ ] Wire up sampling: sampling-rule create --pct=1 --reason="weekday whisper canary"
- [ ] Start 1% exposure, timestamp and owner in notes
- [ ] Run telemetry quick checks every 5/10/15/20 minutes (queries below)
- [ ] Decision at 20m window: continue -> 10% (owner signs), rollback -> run rollback steps and file incident
- [ ] When at 50% and stable for 30m, schedule global flip and update routing pins
- [ ] Post-deploy: kick off nightly eval job and mark release notes (rough template below)

Rollback matrix (short):
- Symptom: 95th latency > 2x baseline for three consecutive 5m buckets -> action: immediate rollback to pre-whisper snapshot and page SRE
- Symptom: error-rate > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline -> action: rollback and open incident (link template)
- Symptom: client-facing hallucination spike (manual detect/alert from QA) -> hold and escalate to applied-ml leads

Telemetry smoke queries (paste into DataDog/Looker/Prometheus)
- p50_latency = query: quantile(0.5, api.latency{route:predict})
- p95_latency = query: quantile(0.95, api.latency{route:predict})
- error_rate = sum(rate(api.errors{route:predict}[5m])) / sum(rate(api.requests{route:predict}[5m]))
- kv_cache_hit = avg(kv.cache_hit_rate{service:serve})
- sampling_token_cost = sum(rate(tokens.consumed{route:predict}[5m])) / sum(rate(api.requests{route:predict}[5m]))

Thresholds (examples we enforce for whisper):
- p95_latency: fail if > baseline_p95 * 2 OR > 4s absolute
- error_rate: fail if delta > +0.5 percentage points OR > 1.0% absolute
- kv_cache_hit: fail if drop > 10% relative

Release notes (roughcut - to be refined before public release)
- Release tag: whisper-2026-06-23-01
- Owner: Riley Nguyen (eng-release-engineering)
- Summary: small model weight and routing tweak to reduce token cost for short-context queries. Changes are behind routing flag and initial 1% canary.
- Impact: expected up to 5% cost savings for inference on short prompts, no schema changes. Internal-only rollout first; external rollouts pending QA results.
- Known risks: subtle latency variance on longer contexts; will monitor p95 and user-facing error rates.
- Rollback plan: revert route pins and restore serving snapshot whisper-pre-20260623.
- Post-deploy checks: run bench-eval/shortprompts and compare scoring metrics; file results to /confluence/whisper-evals.

Quick commands cheatsheet (ops crib)
- snapshot: infra snapshot --name=pre-whisper-$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M)
- sample-on: sampling-rule set --name=whisper-canary --pct=1 --route=canary-route
- sample-up: sampling-rule update --name=whisper-canary --pct=10
- rollback: infra rollback --snapshot=whisper-pre-20260623 --force
- smoke run: ./smoke-tests/run_core_smoke.sh --env=staging --focus=serve

Communication templates (paste to Slack)
- Start announce (short): "STARTING weekday whisper canary: tag=whisper-2026-06-23-01, owner=Riley, pct=1 -> 10. Link dashboard: <link>. OOO unless escalated."
- Progress update: "whisper canary at 10% (t+30m). p95=XXXms, err=YYY%. No action. Proceeding to 50% in 15m if stable."
- Rollback notify: "ROLLBACK executed for whisper-2026-06-23-01 at 10:54 PT. Restored snapshot whisper-pre-20260623. Incident created: <Jira link>."

Post-release quick retro prompts (for <30m debrief)
- Did telemetry match expectations? If not, which metric diverged and why?
- Was the canary window long enough? Any blind spots?
- Were comms clear and timely?
- Action items (owner + due date):
  - fix: add a short-context p95 dashboard panel (owner: Jordan, due: 2026-06-26)
  - improve: automate snapshot naming in infra-cli (owner: Samir, due: 2026-07-01)

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm whether dedicated-pool auto-scaling interacts poorly with partial-route pins (Elena to test).
- Add headless synthetic load generator for long-tail prompt latencies.
- Decide: add additional 5% step between 10% -> 50% for critical serving paths? pros/cons in thread #release-ops.

References / anchors
- Confluence: weekday-release-guidelines (linked above)
- Dashboards: /dashboards/whisper-canary-overview (create if missing)
- Small prompt evals repo: github.com/redwood-inference/mini-evals (PR incoming)

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc minimal and make it the single source for weekday whisper runs. Archive per-release results in the confluence folder and tag the Jira.
- If this pattern proves reliable, propose a short-run SOP to convert into a canonical runbook (eng-release-engineering + SRE).
